findings.title: Backup code plus any totpCode skips password
findings.body: Password is verified only when credentials.totpCode is absent (the condition just above this branch). The new backup-code branch then runs whenever credentials.backupCode is set, and it never checks the password. A request that includes a valid backup code and any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") therefore authenticates with no password at all. Backup codes are meant to replace the authenticator factor, not the password; the login UI still submits the password. Anyone who obtains a backup code (screenshot, downloaded file, clipboard) can mint a session without knowing the account password.

findings.title: Backup codes are compared case-sensitively
findings.body: Codes are generated with crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"), which is lowercase, and both login and the disable endpoint match with indexOf after only stripping dashes. The input placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX", so users will type uppercase. Those codes will be rejected as incorrect even when they are valid, so backup-code login and 2FA disable via backup code fail for normal input. Normalize with toLowerCase() (and trim) before comparing.

findings.title: Download control cannot download the codes
findings.body: The download link wraps a Button that sits inside the enable Form and has no type="button" and no preventDefault. A button defaults to type="submit", so the click submits handleEnable again instead of activating the parent anchor, and a button nested in an <a> does not reliably start the download. Users who just enabled 2FA can be left without a saved copy of codes that are never shown again.

findings.title: Codes are shown only after 2FA is already on, and dismiss loses them
findings.body: handleEnable persists twoFactorEnabled on the server and only then switches to DisplayBackupCodes. onEnable (and thus the parent updating the security page) runs solely from the Close button. Dialog onOpenChange is not intercepted, and resetState does not clear or revoke the codes. Closing the dialog, refreshing, or navigating away after a successful enable leaves 2FA on with the only plaintext copy of the codes discarded and no regenerate API. The user can be locked out of their authenticator recovery path.

findings.title: Enable-and-login e2e never leaves the backup-code step
findings.body: After a correct OTP, enable now stays on the backup-code screen and does not call onEnable until backup-codes-close is clicked. This test never clicks that button (unlike the disable test) and immediately waits for the two-factor switch. The switch state is updated only in onEnable, and the modal is still open, so this test no longer completes a real enable. The new FIXME also admits the isChecked assertion passes even when the switch is unchecked, so the suite will not catch the broken flow.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is overridden
findings.body: PasswordField sets type from isPasswordVisible and then spreads {...props}. This call passes type="password", which overwrites that value, so the show/hide control added by switching this field to PasswordField never reveals the password.

findings.title: Lost access button submits the disable form
findings.body: The new Lost access / Go back button is inside Form and has no type="button". HTML buttons default to submit, so clicking it both toggles the backup-code view and posts handleDisable with whatever totp/backup values are currently registered. That can disable 2FA unintentionally or surface a spurious incorrect-code error while switching modes. Cancel has the same default and should be type="button" as well.
